rejected.reason: Native founder post with visible metrics, but the visible text is only 'And what a day it was!' and relies on quoted context for company specificity. Rejected under the strict self-contained company/founder evidence rule.
Strong first-party founder post, but the exact platformPostId/sourceUrl already exists in src/lib/social/targeted-evidence-current.json.
Native Product Hunt launch/comment-style URL with first-party founder attribution, but the exact URL already exists in src/lib/social/targeted-evidence-current.json.
Not present in targeted-evidence-current.json, but the exact URL was already surfaced in outputs/source-hunt/yc-nonx-fifth-pass.json. Omitted from accepted to keep the ninth pass incremental.
Native HN item with visible metrics, but title is an Ask HN about KugelAudio and the author could not be verified as company, founder, or official account from the local YC identity snapshot.

Native LinkedIn post with visible public snippet, but author is the Y Combinator organization rather than the company, founder, or company official account. Rejected as not first-party under this pass's stricter rule.
Search snippet showed a Drip founder comment, but the available URL is another person's post, not a native Drip founder/company comment URL with comment-level metrics.
Profile page surfaced in search results; profiles are explicitly out of scope even when the profile is a YC-listed founder.
False-positive YouTube match: video is a Y Combinator pitching video, not a native Stage company/founder/official-account post.
False-positive YouTube match: video is an Expanse TV-series clip, not first-party evidence for the YC company Expanse.

searches.queryOrCommand: jq tally of Spring 2026 companies against src/lib/social/targeted-evidence-current.json
searches.result: Current targeted source matched 97 Spring/P26 companies with zero evidence, 43 with one evidence row, 28 with two rows, and 29 with three or more rows. Zero-evidence companies were prioritized.
Built a 292-URL exact current-source dedupe set. All accepted sourceUrl values above were absent from that set.
Accepted the highest-signal official Drip and Zenbu repos with visible GitHub metrics; lower-signal sibling repos were checked but not all were needed in accepted.

searches.queryOrCommand: api.fxtwitter.com/status/{id} for native X leads from search and local graph thumbnails
searches.result: Accepted native founder/company posts with visible metrics and local YC founder/company-account attribution. Rejected one Aseon post whose visible text was too context-dependent.

searches.queryOrCommand: curl YouTube watch pages and /oembed for zero-evidence company launch videos
searches.result: Accepted company/founder-authored videos where watch-page metadata exposed channel, publish date, views, and likes and attribution matched the local YC company/founder snapshot. Memory Store was held out because it had already appeared in a prior source-hunt output.

searches.queryOrCommand: site:linkedin.com/posts and site:x.com searches for Zenbu, Drip, Archer, Astraea, Aster, and Product Hunt variants
searches.result: Found several useful native X URLs and duplicate/non-first-party LinkedIn/Product Hunt leads. LinkedIn YC-org posts and LinkedIn snippets without native first-party comment URLs were rejected.

searches.queryOrCommand: jq review of public/graph/s2026.json product_hunt, hacker_news, youtube, reddit platforms
searches.result: Used local graph rows only as leads, then re-checked native URLs and current metrics before accepting. Rejected HN Ask HN and false-positive YouTube matches where first-party authorship failed.

notes: No source/app JSON files were edited; src/lib/social/targeted-evidence-current.json was read only.
All accepted URLs are absent from the exact sourceUrl set in src/lib/social/targeted-evidence-current.json.

Most accepted entries are for companies with zero current targeted evidence: Zenbu, Drip, Archer, Taiga, Astraea, Lamina Labs, Aseon Labs, Amboras, Humwork, InstaAgent, Arlo Industries, InLoop Robotics, and Fuchsia.
X metrics were captured from FxTwitter public post JSON. GitHub metrics were captured from the GitHub REST repo API. YouTube metrics were captured from watch-page embedded metadata and oEmbed.
No profile pages, search pages, result pages, or inferred profile follower counts were accepted.
